_doc: Stream E (M2). Hidden treasure chains (PLAN §3.7): one STARTING in every zone of Torbor Downs (16), about 1 in 4 crossing 2-3 zones. Every step is a physical clue you find in the world (`clue`: note, map_piece, gravestone, carved_arrow, drunks_story) at a place (`at`: a vignette id, {site: settlement/fort name}, or {landmark: description B's bake turns into a point}), and each clue's text points to the next. The cache shimmers within `shimmer` metres; `how`: dig (needs a tool) or chest (hidden chest). Per-character, server-checked reach (PLAN §11.3).

steps.text: Aled's note mentions he 'buried the rest under the stone that looks like a sleeping dog'.
On the far bank of the ford an arrow is cut into a stone, pointing upstream.

at.landmark: the dog-shaped stone upstream of Fitockpi Ford

cache.hint: Upstream of the ford, a boulder like a curled-up dog.

steps.text: A gravestone in Orrinsford's yard reads: 'Here lies Brother Cole, who counted the coins. He counts them still, twelve paces east of the bell.'
Twelve paces east of the bell: an arrow scratched in the abbey wall, pointing down.

at.landmark: under the abbey wall, below the scratched arrow

cache.hint: Below the arrow on the abbey wall.

steps.text: In a Halsbridge tavern, a drunk swears the old provost hid his purse 'in the miller's second-best wheel'.
Behind the second wheel at Mill End: a torn map piece showing the ford below the mill.

at.landmark: the stepping stones below Mill End

cache.hint: A loose stepping stone below the mill.

steps.text: A torn map piece nailed inside the oldest mill: three circles and an X by a crooked oak.
An arrow carved on Millbrook Keep's gate post points along the north lane.

at.landmark: the crooked oak at the end of the north lane

steps.text: A worn epitaph by the duelling stones: 'Where the keep's shadow falls at noon, my blade sleeps.'
In the Broken Keep's chapel, a monk's note: 'The reliquary went north, up the pass, for safe keeping.'
On the toll fort's oldest stone, the same monk's sign — a little cross and an arrow up the scree.

at.landmark: a hermit's niche in the scree above Hollin Toll Fort

cache.hint: A niche in the scree above the fort.

steps.text: Old Pike, three ales in, says his grandad hid 'the good stuff' down the dry well and 'the better stuff' where the lamps are lit last.
On the dry well's ledge: a map piece showing Pickaxe Row's last lamp post.

at.landmark: beneath the last lamp post on Pickaxe Row

steps.text: Wenna's uncle tells of an 'eel queen' who wore a tin crown and hid it from the taxman in the witch's garden.
A note under a jar in the witch's garden: 'Crown's in the tower, top step, the creaky one. — M.'

cache.hint: The creaky top step of Reedwall Tower.

steps.text: Pinned under a rock on Gull Steps: half a map with a cove and a cross.
In the smugglers' cellar, a ledger page: 'Rest of the take went to the lakes, to the stilt fort, under the third stilt.'
The third stilt of the Stilt Fort bears a carved anchor.

at.landmark: in the mud beneath the third stilt of the Stilt Fort

steps.text: The old ferryman never spent a copper in his life, Nell says. 'He kept 'em by the shrine, for luck.'
Behind the drowned shrine's pillar, a little carved boat points across the water.

at.landmark: the islet across from the drowned shrine

cache.hint: On the islet across the water.

steps.text: The hermit's diary, left open: 'Buried my past by the boars, where nobody sane goes.'
At the boar wallow, an arrow carved into an oak root.

at.landmark: under the marked oak root by the boar wallow

steps.text: Garrick the pedlar, after a jug, says Widow Edda's dowry was sent north 'to the wolds, to be safe from raiders' and never came back.
In the ash of the first barn, a scorched receipt: 'One chest, carried to Lowmoor, left with the bastion keeper.'
A carved heart-and-arrow on the bastion's postern points down the bank to the river.

at.landmark: the river bank below the Mossy Bastion

cache.hint: The bank below the bastion's postern.

steps.text: A captured raider's orders: 'Pay chest stays at the burned farm until the vale road clears.'
A raider's mark burned into Cinder Farm's gatepost, pointing west toward Millbrook Vale.
Tucked in a crack of Millbrook Keep's gate: a raider's map piece, an X in the gorse behind the keep.

at.landmark: in the gorse behind Millbrook Keep

cache.hint: In the gorse behind the keep.

steps.text: Jory the penitent swears the cult keeps its offerings 'where the thorns grow in a ring'.
A lantern-keeper's stone: 'I lit the ring of thorns once. It did not like it.'

at.landmark: inside the ring of thorns north of Last Lantern

steps.text: A tollkeeper's grave: 'Honest to the last. Mostly. Look where the goats won't go.'
An arrow on the fort's outer wall points up the scree.

at.landmark: the ledge up the scree where the goats won't go

steps.text: Pike of Netherby says his father dropped 'a fortune in a sack' off the jetty and could never find it.
The tower's old chart marks the jetty with a little sack.

at.landmark: off the end of Netherby jetty, at low water

cache.hint: Off the end of the jetty when the water's low.

steps.text: Under moss on the bastion wall: 'Vault key with the lurkers. Vault with the mushrooms.'
A digger's arrow at Deepdene points into the mushroom hollows.

at.landmark: in the mushroom hollow east of Lowmoor
